scope: Targeted primary-source context for AP with incomplete labels, finite-population resampling and completion bounds. Not a systematic review or priority search.
source_selection: Publisher pages, original author-hosted papers, one explicitly author-uploaded paper, official methodological report, and original software documentation. Search aggregators were used only for discovery.
quotation_policy: Each source has at most one short verbatim support excerpt, below 25 words. Supporting paraphrases remain below 200 words per source; no paper copies are redistributed.

sources.citation: Household Finance and Consumption Network (2023). Household Finance and Consumption Survey: Methodological report for the 2021 wave. ECB Statistics Paper Series 45.
sources.primary_source: Official report, full PDF and rendered formula pages inspected
sources.location: Section 7.2, printed pages 52–53; PDF zero-based pages 55–56; section 7.2.1
sources.short_exact_support: out of which 𝑛ℎ are sampled without replacement
sources.supports: For strata sampled without replacement, w*=w(1-lambda+lambda*n/m*r), lambda=sqrt(m*(1-f)/(n-1)); section 7.2.1 sets m=n-1. This gives the implemented positive-baseline finite-correction weights.
sources.does_not_support: A finite-sample AP percentile coverage theorem, a universal rare-positive cutoff, or inference over new projects.
sources.recommended_use: Keep R3 reference 19 for weight provenance; distinguish report year 2023 from survey wave 2021.

sources.citation: Yilmaz, E.; Aslam, J.A. (2008). Estimating average precision when judgments are incomplete. Knowledge and Information Systems 16, 173–211.
sources.primary_source: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record; subscription full text not inspected
sources.short_exact_support: when relevance judgments are a random subset of complete judgments
sources.supports: Induced AP, subcollection AP and inferred AP address statistical estimation of AP from incomplete relevance judgments; incomplete-label AP evaluation is established prior work.
sources.does_not_support: The present grouped-threshold completion DP, arbitrary unresolved semantic labels being missing at random, or coverage of this implementation.
sources.recommended_use: Keep R3 reference 18 as concise related context. Cite the volume year 2008; 14 August 2007 is online publication, not a conflicting edition.

sources.citation: Yilmaz, E.; Kanoulas, E.; Aslam, J.A. (2008). A Simple and Efficient Sampling Method for Estimating AP and NDCG. SIGIR 2008, 603–610.
sources.primary_source: Publisher indexed abstract corroborated by full original paper explicitly uploaded by coauthor Evangelos Kanoulas; author-hosted Northeastern PDF retrieval was blocked
sources.supports: Prior work already combines incomplete-judgment AP estimation, stratified random sampling and confidence intervals.
sources.does_not_support: Identifying infAP with sklearn sample-weighted AP, substituting its intervals without verifying design/estimator compatibility, or sharp completion bounds.
sources.recommended_use: Optional if R3 discusses survey-style AP estimation more broadly. Not needed merely to increase reference count.

sources.citation: Boyd, K.; Eng, K.H.; Page, C.D. (2013). Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve: Point Estimates and Confidence Intervals. ECML PKDD 2013, LNAI 8190, 451–466.
sources.primary_source: Corrected author-hosted full paper and publisher metadata inspected
sources.location: Sections 3.2 and 4.2; corrected interpolation integral footnote on fifth PDF page
sources.short_exact_support: we recommend using stratified bootstrap so π is preserved exactly in all replicates
sources.supports: Earlier simulation work evaluated AUCPR point/interval estimators and reported bootstrap undercoverage in its studied settings. Its resampling fixes class counts and targets distributional AUCPR.
sources.does_not_support: Calibration of the current finite-frame weighted AP procedure, automatic replacement by binomial/logit intervals, or attribution of the exact 514/969 counterexample to this paper.
sources.recommended_use: Optional short uncertainty-context citation. If generic bootstrap fragility is described as a contribution, explicitly acknowledge this earlier context.

sources.citation: Boyd, K.; Eng, K.H.; Page, C.D. (2013). Erratum: Area under the Precision-Recall Curve: Point Estimates and Confidence Intervals. LNAI 8190, E1.
sources.primary_source: Publisher correction text and coauthor institutional record; corrected equation also checked in author paper
sources.location: Erratum abstract, referring to bottom of printed page 455
sources.supports: The correction concerns the interpolated PR-area integral, not bibliographic metadata. The corrected antiderivative is (a*r-b*log(a*r+b))/a^2 in the stated nondegenerate case.
sources.does_not_support: A correction to the present noninterpolated AP definition or a retraction of the paper's coverage experiment.
sources.recommended_use: Track with Boyd if cited; do not reproduce the uncorrected interpolation expression. The current DP never uses this interpolation.

sources.citation: Urlus, R.E.Q.; Baak, M.A.; Collot, S.; Fridman Rojas, I. (2023). Pointwise sampling uncertainties on the Precision-Recall curve. PMLR 206, AISTATS 2023.
sources.primary_source: Original proceedings paper, full PDF inspected
sources.location: Sections 1–3, especially iid multinomial confusion-matrix assumption on third PDF page
sources.short_exact_support: the confusion matrix of an i.i.d. sample
sources.supports: Pointwise precision/recall uncertainty is a distinct problem with an explicit sampling model.
sources.does_not_support: A confidence interval for integrated AP under unequal-probability finite-population sampling, or automatic simultaneous coverage of an entire curve.
sources.recommended_use: Optional boundary clarification only; no need to expand R3 with this separate method.

sources.citation: scikit-learn developers. average_precision_score API documentation. Accessed 26 October 2026.
sources.supports: AP is the sum of threshold precision times recall increments; it differs from trapezoidal PR area. This matches the grouped-threshold convention used by the DP.
sources.does_not_support: Unknown-label inference, random tie-breaking AP, or treating sklearn's no-positive convention as the study's scientific definition.
sources.recommended_use: Definition/provenance support; retain the study's explicit undefined P=0 contract and frozen software version.

additional_primary_context_not_required_.citation: Imbens, G.W.; Manski, C.F. (2004). Confidence Intervals for Partially Identified Parameters. Econometrica 72(6), 1845–1857.
additional_primary_context_not_required_.verification: Publisher abstract retrieved. Distinguishes an identification region from confidence procedures accounting for estimated-bound sampling variation. This general conceptual context does not prove the present finite-score DP or license transferring a CI formula.
